The two never-lifts cleanup tests assert only `isinstance(cleanup, PermissionError)`, so an unrelated `PermissionError` would pass. Task 10's contract asked for the exact type and the injected object or message. **DEFER (verified, single-voice)**: confirmed at lines 435 and 464; the injector raises `PermissionError(errno.EACCES, "read-only file refused deletion", path)`, so `type(cleanup) is PermissionError` plus `cleanup.strerror` would close it. The PRD rule (keep the original as the raised error) is met and pinned by identity. The installed gate refuses a single-voice task, so this is carried to batch end as a test-strength follow-up. Alice's "exact `PermissionError` context" claim is refuted by the code.
